desc:
An IPv6 address is written as eight groups separated by single colons. A group is 1 to 4 hexadecimal digits (0-9, a-f, A-F); leading zeros may be dropped, so 0 and 0db8 are both fine.

To shorten an address, one run of one or more consecutive all-zero groups may be replaced by a double colon ::. The double colon may appear at the start, in the middle or at the end, and it can be used at most once.

Return true if s is a valid IPv6 address in this notation, otherwise false. Embedded IPv4 forms are not considered.

Valid: 2001:db8:85a3:0:0:8a2e:370:7334, 2001:db8::1, ::, ::1, 1::, 1:2:3:4:5:6:7::. Invalid: 1:2:3:4:5:6:7 (only seven groups, no ::), 1::2::3 (two double colons), :::, 1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8:: (eight groups plus :: leaves nothing to compress), :1:2:3:4:5:6:7 (single leading colon), 12345:: (group too long), g::.
constraints: s contains letters, digits and colons only
hints: Without any :: the rule is simple: split on :, expect exactly 8 groups, and validate each group.
With a ::, split the string around it into a left and a right part, split each part on single colons, and validate those groups. How many explicit groups may remain?

The :: must stand for at least one group, so at most 7 explicit groups are allowed. Reject a second :: and also :::. A lone colon at the start or end leaves an empty group, which fails group validation automatically.
editorial: Handle the two shapes separately. If the string contains no ::, it must split on : into exactly eight groups, each of 1-4 hex digits. If it contains ::, it may contain it only once and not as part of :::. Split once around the double colon; the left and right parts are each either empty or a colon-separated list of groups. The compressed run covers at least one group, so the total number of explicit groups must be at most 7.

Empty pieces are the main trap and the reason the split-based approach works so well: a string like 1:2:: splits into left 1:2 and an empty right side (no groups), which is fine, while :1::2 yields the left group list ['', '1'] whose empty group is rejected, because a single leading colon is not allowed.
Each character is inspected a constant number of times, so the time is O(n).
